## Project 2 Interim Data Analysis Plan

### Requirements
1. For each aim, the hypotheses you will be testing, including a description of the outcome(s) and predictor(s) of interest

2. The over-all analysis approach you will be using for each hypothesis

3. How you will approach/incorporate the other data/variables available besides the outcomes and predictors of interest

4. What power/sample size calculations you will conduct for each of the hypotheses of interest

5. Not required for interim, but will be required for final: thoughts on your approach to type I error control.

### Aim 1

We hypothesize that higher levels of inflammation at baseline, as indicated by cytokine and chemokine levels in circulating plasma, will predict declines in clinical memory measures and decreases in cortical thickness, another marker of memory function. Furthermore, greater increases in cytokines and chemokine levels between year 0 and year 1 will be associated with greater declines in memory measures and cortical thickness. To test for association between baseline inflammation levels and memory decline, we will use general linear models between the measured cytokine and chemokines, MCP-1, Eotaxin-1, IL-6, and TNF-alpha, and the change in each measure of memory, as well as cortical thickness, between year 0 and year 1. The four memory measures we will model are a list learning measure, figure recall, the mnemonic similarity task, and long term consolidation. We will adjust for age, sex, APOE genotype, clinical dementia rating, and geriatric depression measure as precision variables, along with immunological health conditions and cardiovascular risk as potential confounders. We will also perform data exploration to identify any other health measures that may be correlated with the outcomes and include them if necessary. The same covariates and outcomes will be used to test the hypothesis that increases in cytokine and chemokine levels between year 0 and year 1 result in declines in memory function.

We will perform power calculations using a correlation test. 



### Aim 2
We will test our hypothesis of an interaction between peripheral levels of inflammation and amyloid deposition,
such that the presence of both significant amyloid deposition and elevated peripheral inflammatory markers will
be the strongest predictors of memory decline and decline in AD-signature cortical thickness over a one year
period.
